<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Enable Helion across KDA prefill, decode, and EAGLE/MTP verification for models such as GLM-5.3-Flash. The existing prefill adapter omits the raw-beta flag, bounded-gate decode bypasses the Helion packed kernel, and Helion target verification is missing.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Forward `beta_is_raw` in the Helion prefill adapter.
- Enable Helion packed decode for bounded-gate KDA.
- Add Helion chain/tree verification with per-candidate state snapshots and register the verify backend.
- Add numerical and dispatcher regression tests, including CUDA Graph coverage.

Existing backend defaults are unchanged. MTP verification uses state snapshots; ReplaySSM verification is outside this PR's scope.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Validated GLM-5.3-Flash on 4 × H200 with Helion 1.4.0, using Helion for all three KDA phases and EAGLE with 5 steps, top-k 1, and 6 draft tokens.

GSM8K: 100 examples, 5-shot, 8 threads, two runs, max tokens 4096, temperature 0, `reasoning_effort=low`.

| Configuration | Run 1 | Run 2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Helion prefill + decode + verify, MTP516 | 99% | 99% |

Passed 11 GPU tests and 9 dispatcher tests (plus 5 subtests), covering numerical correctness, state snapshots, chain/tree verification, and CUDA Graph replay. Pre-commit checks passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

Benchmarked GLM-5.3-Flash with PyTorch 2.14.1, Triton 3.8.0, and Helion 1.4.0. Both configurations use MTP516 and Prefill/Decode CUDA Graphs; each A/B comparison changes only the three KDA backend flags.

| Configuration | 4 × H200 | 4 × B200 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parallelism | TP4 / EP4 | TP4 / EP4 |
| DSA prefill / decode | TileLang | TRTLLM |
| KV dtype | BF16 | FP8 E4M3 |
| MoE runner | DeepGEMM | FlashInfer TRTLLM |
| Prefill CUDA Graph | Breakable, max tokens 8192 | Breakable, GLM default max tokens 4096 |

H200 TP4/EP1 launch command (replace the three `helion` backend values with `triton` for the comparison):

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash \
  --served-model-name llm \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --ep-size 4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.75 \
  --max-mamba-cache-size 240 \
  --max-running-requests 48 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 8192 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 48 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang \
  --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --linear-attn-prefill-backend helion \
  --linear-attn-decode-backend helion \
  --linear-attn-verify-backend helion \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --moe-a2a-backend none \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 8090
```

**End-to-end throughput:** median of three runs after warmup, using `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random`, fixed input/output lengths, temperature 0, seed 42, and ignore EOS. C1/C16/C48 use 8/64/192 requests per run. All completed benchmark requests succeeded.

**End-to-end throughput:** median of three runs after warmup, using `sglang.benchmark.serving --dataset-name random`, fixed input/output lengths, temperature 0, seed 42, and ignore EOS. C1/C16/C48 use 8/64/192 requests per run. All completed benchmark requests succeeded.

| GPU | Input / Output | Concurrency | Triton tok/s | Helion tok/s | Change |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| H200 | 4096 / 1024 | 1 | 438.42 | 442.10 | +0.84% |
| H200 | 4096 / 1024 | 16 | 2525.64 | 2508.28 | -0.69% |
| H200 | 4096 / 1024 | 48 | 3607.69 | 3600.08 | -0.21% |
| H200 | 32768 / 1024 | 1 | 264.85 | 264.41 | -0.17% |
| H200 | 32768 / 1024 | 16 | 668.92 | 666.20 | -0.41% |
| B200 | 4096 / 1024 | 1 | 625.86 | 638.65 | +2.04% |
| B200 | 4096 / 1024 | 16 | 3354.40 | 3401.47 | +1.40% |
| B200 | 4096 / 1024 | 48 | 5043.03 | 5144.58 | +2.01% |
| B200 | 32768 / 1024 | 1 | 374.27 | 378.42 | +1.11% |
| B200 | 32768 / 1024 | 16 | 921.27 | 915.25 | -0.65% |

Helion throughput is within ±1% of Triton on H200. On B200, it improves throughput by 1.1–2.0% in four workloads and is 0.65% lower at 32K input with concurrency 16.

**KDA microbenchmarks:** single GPU, 16 heads with head dimension 128, BF16 inputs, FP32 state, and bounded gate −5. Median CUDA Graph replay latency after warmup, excluding compilation and input/state resets. Outputs and state snapshots were checked against Triton.

| Phase | Batch × tokens/request | H200 Triton µs | H200 Helion µs | Change | B200 Triton µs | B200 Helion µs | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| prefill | 1 × 4096 | 386.11 | 428.40 | +10.95% | 364.54 | 391.17 | +7.30% |
| prefill | 1 × 8192 | 750.29 | 820.59 | +9.37% | 710.66 | 749.60 | +5.48% |
| prefill | 2 × 4096 | 631.42 | 666.61 | +5.57% | 571.39 | 606.19 | +6.09% |
| decode | 1 × 1 | 7.20 | 6.05 | -16.00% | 8.22 | 6.16 | -25.10% |
| decode | 16 × 1 | 14.78 | 11.28 | -23.70% | 16.38 | 10.21 | -37.70% |
| decode | 48 × 1 | 40.80 | 29.54 | -27.61% | 22.53 | 18.40 | -18.32% |
| verify | 1 × 6 | 18.69 | 12.16 | -34.93% | 20.48 | 14.37 | -29.84% |
| verify | 16 × 6 | 38.94 | 44.11 | +13.27% | 34.78 | 32.80 | -5.70% |
| verify | 48 × 6 | 109.07 | 113.95 | +4.47% | 90.11 | 79.87 | -11.36% |

Negative latency changes indicate lower latency. Helion reduces packed-decode latency by **16–28% on H200 and 18–38% on B200**. Prefill is slower in the tested shapes, while verify performance varies by hardware and batch size.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

detail.title: [KDA] Support Helion MTP verification and harden prefill, decode

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,145 @@
+"""Helion KDA verification with per-candidate state snapshots."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import helion
+import helion.language as hl
+import torch
+
+
+@helion.kernel(
+    static_shapes=False,
+    config=helion.Config(
+        block_sizes=[8],
+        num_warps=1,
+        num_stages=1,
+        indexing="pointer",
+    ),
+    ignore_warnings=[helion.exc.ProcessGroupNameNotFound],
+)
+def _kda_verify(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    v: torch.Tensor,
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    b: torch.Tensor,
+    A_log: torch.Tensor,
+    dt_bias: torch.Tensor,
+    state_pool: torch.Tensor,
+    state_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+    snapshots: torch.Tensor,
+    snapshot_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    parents: torch.Tensor | None,
+    out: torch.Tensor,
+    lower_bound: float,
+    bounded_gate: hl.constexpr,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    N = cu_seqlens.size(0) - 1
+    H = hl.specialize(q.size(1))
+    HV = hl.specialize(v.size(1))
+    K = hl.specialize(q.size(2))
+    V = hl.specialize(v.size(2))
+    block_v = hl.register_block_size(1, V)
+    for tile_n, tile_h, tile_v in hl.tile([N, HV, V], block_size=[1, 1, block_v]):
+        n, hv = tile_n.id, tile_h.id
+        h = hv // (HV // H)
+        keys = hl.arange(K)
+        slot = state_indices[n].long()
+        scratch = snapshot_indices[n].long()
+        start = cu_seqlens[n].long()
+        end = cu_seqlens[n + 1].long()
+        state = hl.load(
+            state_pool, [slot, hv, tile_v.index, keys], extra_mask=slot >= 0
+        ).float()
+        for token in range(start, end):
+            step = token - start
+            if parents is not None:
+                use_parent = (step > 0) & (scratch >= 0)
+                parent = parents[n, step].long()
+                parent_state = hl.load(
+                    snapshots,
+                    [scratch, parent, hv, tile_v.index, keys],
+                    extra_mask=use_parent,
+                ).float()
+                state = torch.where(use_parent, parent_state, state)
+            raw_gate = a[token, hv, keys].float() + dt_bias[hv, keys].float()
+            A = torch.exp(A_log[hv].float())
+            if bounded_gate:
+                log_decay = lower_bound * torch.sigmoid(A * raw_gate)
+            else:
+                softplus = torch.where(
+                    raw_gate <= 20.0, torch.log(1.0 + torch.exp(raw_gate)), raw_gate
+                )
+                log_decay = -A * softplus
+            beta = torch.sigmoid(b[token, hv].float())
+            query = q[token, h, keys].float()
+            key = k[token, h, keys].float()
+            query = query / torch.sqrt((query * query).sum() + 1e-6)
+            key = key / torch.sqrt((key * key).sum() + 1e-6)
+            state = state * torch.exp(log_decay)[None, :]
+            value = v[token, hv, tile_v].float()
+            residual = (value - (state * key[None, :]).sum(-1)) * beta
+            state = state + residual[:, None] * key[None, :]
+            out[token, hv, tile_v] = (state * (query * K**-0.5)[None, :]).sum(-1)
+            if scratch >= 0:
+                snapshots[scratch, step, hv, tile_v.index, keys] = state
+    return out
+
+
+def helion_kda_verify(
+    *,
+    q: torch.Tensor,

Thanks for the suggestion! I reran the H200 verify microbenchmarks with thorough warmup across three independent processes, alternating the backend order. The results reproduce the same trend:

Batch × tokens/request | Triton (μs) | Helion (μs) | Latency change
-- | -- | -- | --
1 × 6 | 18.624 | 12.384 | −33.51%
16 × 6 | 39.120 | 44.848 | +14.64%
48 × 6 | 108.768 | 114.048 | +4.85%

Each backend/shape had 1,500 measured samples in total. Output and state-snapshot comparisons passed, and the run-to-run median latency variation was below 0.47% for B16/B48.
Helion remains faster at B1, but slower at B16/B48 for these H200 verify shapes. The repeated measurements suggest this is a consistent performance difference rather than measurement noise; the underlying cause still needs investigation.
